vocabularyMapping.hazard: The word 'Final' means OPPOSITE things in new17's F1 and in the upstream versioning vocabulary. Reading upstream's 'not Final' as an F1 failure imports someone else's vocabulary into our criterion.
vocabularyMapping.upstreamFinalMeans: past, complete specifications that will not be changed (i.e. frozen and superseded)
vocabularyMapping.f1FinalMeans: published and citable rather than draft/RC
vocabularyMapping.measured: 2026-07-28 is upstream 'Current'. Under upstream's vocabulary it is deliberately NOT 'Final'; under F1's criterion it PASSES.
vocabularyMapping.consequence: A future reader of this file must not invert F1 by applying the upstream glossary to it.

That property's own description carries the transport requirement verbatim: the value MUST match the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header, and the server MUST return a `400 Bad Request` otherwise. The consequence travels with the requirement, which is what makes it normative rather than descriptive.

$defs.UnsupportedProtocolVersionError pins error.code const -32022 under allOf[1], and error.data requires [requested, supported] — the same constant server.ts serves as ERR.UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION.
$defs.CacheableResult carries cacheScope (private|public) and a TTL hint, covering the `cache` third of this gate's requirement line.

gates.qualifier: normative but NOT part of core

evidence.observation: Tasks are specified as an EXTENSION: opt-in, negotiated during initialization. The semantics are normative within the extension; a core-only implementation is conformant without them.
evidence.consequence: Any future CallLint claim about task semantics must be scoped to the extension, never stated as core protocol support.

amendedByM26-8.verdict: PASS stands, and it is now GATE-BACKED — by an ABSENCE, which is the stronger form of this claim.
amendedByM26-8.supersedes: The `evidence.source` above is a URL no gate in this repository can re-read. Read THIS block's `source` as current; the URL is retained verbatim as the record of where the claim was first measured.
amendedByM26-8.whyAnAbsenceIsStronger: The observation above says tasks are an extension, so a core-only implementation is conformant without them. Read on the extension page, that is upstream's prose about its own scoping. Read in the locked core schema, it is a measured absence: ZERO task-named $defs, ZERO occurrences of `tasks/` as a method namespace, and exactly ONE case-insensitive `task` hit — an example identifier inside $defs.ServerCapabilities.properties.extensions.description, which is itself the proof that tasks are opt-in. The core schema does not merely say tasks are optional; it does not define them at all.
amendedByM26-8.absenceVacuityDiscipline: An absence asserted against an unparsed or empty object passes trivially. The gate therefore asserts the schema parsed and carries exactly 155 $defs BEFORE any of the three absences above, and pins the single `task` hit's location so that a future re-vendor introducing real task semantics reds instead of satisfying the absence with a renamed def.
amendedByM26-8.whyItWasWrong: Nothing in the observation above was false. What was wrong was its PROVENANCE: transcribed from a rendered page, unre-derivable by any CI run. subClaimOverPrecise.asRecorded: The earliest possible removal is the first revision on or after 2027-07-28.
subClaimOverPrecise.asMeasured: True of 4 of the 6 rows. `includeContext: "thisServer"/"allServers"` reads 'Follows Sampling (SEP-2577)', and HTTP+SSE transport reads 'Three months after SEP-2596 reaches Final' — a date the registry does not record and that this repository cannot compute.
subClaimOverPrecise.whyTheVerdictSurvives: F7 asks whether a breaking ERRATUM is pending, and deprecation is not removal. Upstream states a Deprecated feature 'remains part of the specification but is scheduled for removal', that earliest removal only marks ELIGIBILITY, and that the actual removal is a Core Maintainer decision taken during release preparation — i.e. an act of a FUTURE revision. The Removed section is empty. So nothing breaks within 2026-07-28 on either clock, and the unrecorded SEP-2596 date cannot move the verdict; it bounds only how precisely the sentence may be phrased.
subClaimOverPrecise.forwardObligation: Any future CallLint copy about 2026-07-28 deprecations must not state a single uniform removal date. Two of the six clocks are relative, and one of those two depends on an upstream event with no published date.

nonClaimsAmendedByM26-4.whyThisIsRecordedRatherThanJustDeleted: `nonClaims` had ZERO machine readers — measured: `grep -rn 'nonClaims' --include=*.ts --include=*.mjs` returns only this file. So all three entries could go stale silently, which is precisely the defect M26-3 (ADR 0065) was built to end, recurring one field away from the reader it installed. M26-3's gate reads `verdict`, `productionChangesAllowed`, and the eight gate rows; it does not read this list. That is the general lesson restated with a new instance: a reader covers the fields it names, and the fields beside them keep drifting.
